_comment: Which result artifacts are current. Read by tests/test_artifact_staleness.py. The canonical path under artifacts/{audit,m3,m4,m5a} always holds the current run. A superseded artifact is moved under artifacts/superseded/<why>/ and kept, because the append-only EXPERIMENT_LOG.md cites its numbers; nothing new may cite it. An unstamped artifact carries no record of the code that wrote it and is listed with the reason that is tolerable, as a ratchet: stamp the script, re-run, remove the entry.

artifacts/superseded/pre_yawfix/audit/ma.reason: Written 2026-09-28, before the 2026-10-04 yaw fix in seam.features.markers. Its head_shake prevalence (0.785) and the negation/head_shake association derived from it are artifacts of the broken decomposition.

artifacts/superseded/pre_yawfix/audit/co.reason: Written 2026-09-27, before both head-path changes (the 2026-09-28 oscillation-threshold fix and the 2026-10-04 yaw fix). Its head_shake rows (251 pairs / 210 clips) and head_nod rows (13 / 9) do not survive: re-run, each has 1 pair. The four blendshape rows are identical in the successor.

artifacts/superseded/pre_yawfix/m4/facto.reason: The single-expression framing (314 of 1,765 windows), superseded on 2026-09-28 by the multi-label run, and also pre-yaw-fix.
Written 2026-10-01, before the yaw fix. Each window's frame was chosen by brow_raise + head_shake evidence, so the inputs changed when head_shake did.
Written 2026-10-01, before the yaw fix; same frame-selection dependence as the heuristic-label run.

artifacts/superseded/yawfix_softmax_sele.reason: Yaw-fixed inputs, but checkpoints were still selected on a softmax cross-entropy over the multi-label affect logits and the entangled baseline was trained without the factorized model's class and positive-label weights. Kept because it isolates the effect of the yaw fix alone.
As above, the three-seed ablation grid.
As above, the single-seed ablation grid; seed 0 is contained in the three-seed successor.

artifacts/superseded/one_to_one_frame_ma.reason: Two defects. Token frames were mapped frame-for-frame although the indices are on a 30 fps timeline and 138 of 200 clips are 24 fps, so most tokens were read from the wrong frames; and the classifier (ridge 1.0 on unstandardised features) predicted one gloss in every fold, on real and shuffled labels alike, so its WER equalled the most-frequent baseline by construction.

Reported 89.5% / 89.9% of tokens 'aligned' under the frame-for-frame mapping. In range is not aligned: the successor tests the mapping against an independent signal. The frame-rate-aware in-range counts are in artifacts/data/asllrp_alignment.json.

artifacts/superseded/before_stamping/aud.reason: Same script and inputs, written before artifacts carried a provenance stamp. Kept only so the M1 log lines that cite it trace to a file if a re-run differs in the last digit.

artifacts/superseded/before_stamping/m3/.reason: Same script and inputs, written before artifacts carried a provenance stamp.

artifacts/superseded/head_axes_2026-10-0.reason: First marker validation, 2026-10-05. Its heuristic and 61-feature rows are reproduced unchanged in the current file; it lacks the second design (page detector, tuned detector, compact fitted detector) that reads head turn for head_shake and head nod for head_nod. seam.features.markers reads tilt and turn for those two, which is why this file scored both at 0.50.

artifacts/superseded/one_hand_wrong_axis.reason: Computed before two defects were corrected on 2026-10-05: the perception stack filed one hand in both hand slots (two identical one-hand graphs), and seam.features.markers read a head tilt for head_shake and a head turn for head_nod. Kept because EXPERIMENT_LOG entries up to that date cite its numbers.
